smell: SetupKubeconfig performs filesystem I/O (FileExists, env mutation) but omits context.Context, while every other exported method on *Phase (Execute, DeployInfrastructure, WaitForBootstrap, MonitorInstallation, SetupClusterAccess, StartWorkerVMs, ValidateClusterAccess) takes ctx first. The asymmetry blocks callers from cancelling the sequence uniformly and breaks ctx-first discipline on the exported Phase surface.
severity_reason: Minimal current-harm (filesystem op is fast) but the signature is out of family with sibling Phase methods and blocks future I/O (writing a sentinel) from honoring cancellation.
fix_summary: Change signature to `func (p *Phase) SetupKubeconfig(ctx context.Context, clusterDir string) error`. Update the single call site in internal/distribution/okd/install/steps.go:64 to pass ctx. Matches SetupClusterAccess in the same phase (which takes ctx even though it currently ignores it).
rule_source: Google Go Style Guide §Contexts ('context.Context should be the first argument of exported functions that do I/O or may block')
must_preserve: Canonical call site at install/steps.go StepSetupKubeconfig; must still mutate p.Exec.Env so downstream subprocesses inherit KUBECONFIG.

smell: firewall.Configure and firewall.RemoveRules are exported but every in-tree caller uses ConfigureOKD / RemoveOKDRules. RemoveRules(HAProxyFrontendPorts(), ...) is the one exception — a single call in postinstall/haproxy.go. Configure has no direct caller. The pair is shaped like a 'future distro swap' API; flag as scaffolding, noting Configure is unreferenced.
severity_reason: Scaffolding-shaped: if Configure exists, RemoveRules stays; they map to a future 'configure arbitrary port set' CLI path (symmetric API).
fix_summary: Verify intent — are Configure/RemoveRules expected entry points for a future non-OKD distro? If yes, keep and document the layering. If no, inline Configure into ConfigureOKD and keep RemoveRules (still has one external caller).
rule_source: MEMORY.md §scaffolding (symmetric API: Configure exists, RemoveRules stays)
CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (package-level helpers live in producer pkg)
must_preserve: validatePort allowlist; both wrappers' current behavior.

smell: cleanup.GenerateSummary and cleanup.Summary struct are exported but the only caller is the package-private printSummary(). No external caller. The function is shaped like a public status-query but without a symmetric sibling (no cleanup.Verify or similar), so it does not cleanly fit scaffolding.
severity_reason: Possibly shaped for a future `okdctl cleanup status` CLI verb; defer to owner rather than deleting. No correctness impact.
fix_summary: Either unexport (GenerateSummary -> generateSummary, Summary -> summary) if no CLI surface planned, or keep both exported and add a one-line doc-comment pointing to the intended caller (e.g. 'used by okdctl cleanup status; see roadmap.md').
rule_source: Uber §Exported Surface ('do not export without a caller')
MEMORY.md §scaffolding (not symmetric — no matching verb in cleanup/)
must_preserve: The current behavior when printSummary runs at the end of Execute.

smell: OKDVersionFetcher.GetLatestStable and OKDVersionFetcher.GetLatestForMinor remain exported with no caller. Only FetchVersions is invoked (internal/cli/releases.go:116). Both are shaped like a symmetric-API trio (FetchVersions / GetLatestStable / GetLatestForMinor) for a future `okdctl releases latest [--minor N.M]` verb.
severity_reason: Scaffolding: symmetric API with a single consumed member (FetchVersions). Future CLI verb 'releases latest' is a plausible caller.
fix_summary: Verify intent against roadmap.md — if a `okdctl releases latest [--minor N.M]` command is planned, keep both. Otherwise demote to private helpers. Do not delete without checking with owner.
must_preserve: FetchVersions (has a caller) and the disk cache behavior.

smell: Phase.ValidateClusterAccess, Phase.SetupClusterAccess, Phase.SetupKubeconfig remain exported with callers only inside the same package's steps.go. Since Phase is itself exported and these are phase-public methods called by a user-facing okd.Provisioner, they fit a future-CLI-verb shape ('okdctl cluster access verify', 'okdctl kubeconfig-setup'). Flagged as scaffolding.
severity_reason: Scaffolding: shaped like future-CLI-verb (e.g. `okdctl cluster access verify`). Keeping per MEMORY.md §scaffolding.
fix_summary: Verify intent — do any planned subcommands call these? If yes, keep exported and document. If no, unexport (validateClusterAccess) to reduce package surface.
must_preserve: The step.go callers' behavior; the deploy-time chown semantics in SetupClusterAccess.

smell: setup.DefaultOptions continues the Default* naming pattern common for 'zero-arg constructor of a defaulted options struct'. Other phase packages use NewOptions(cfg, projectRoot). The same repo also has install.DefaultBootstrapTimeout (constant) — a reader can't tell whether Default*-prefixed symbols are values or functions at a glance.
severity_reason: Naming consistency. Rename to setup.NewOptions(cfg, projectRoot) and the three *Options factories all share the same name.
fix_summary: Rename setup.DefaultOptions -> setup.NewOptions; accept (cfg, projectRoot) and fold any cfg-driven defaults inside. Single call site in okd.go updates. Aligns with opt-inconsistent-cfg-opts finding.
rule_source: Go naming convention: `New*` for constructors; `Default*` for values

smell: ValidateIgnitionFiles is exported, opens three files with os.Stat / os.ReadFile, and omits ctx. Called from within GenerateIgnitionConfigs which has a ctx, so threading it through is cheap. Matches the Setup Phase family where every other exported method takes ctx as first arg.
severity_reason: Exported method doing I/O without ctx — breaks ctx-first discipline. Low current-harm (local FS) but blocks cancellation on a future remote-path variant and is out of family with sibling exports.
fix_summary: Change signature to `func (p *Phase) ValidateIgnitionFiles(ctx context.Context, clusterDir string) error`. The single in-package caller at ignition.go:171 already has ctx. No external caller to update.
must_preserve: Validation semantics: require bootstrap/master/worker.ign ≥ 1KiB, each valid JSON.

smell: GenerateTerraformVars is exported, writes terraform.tfvars via renderAndWrite (filesystem I/O), and omits ctx. Every other exported method on setup.Phase takes ctx as first arg. Called from setup/steps.go:234 which has a ctx.
severity_reason: Exported I/O method out of family; cancellation cannot propagate to an eventual long-running template-render or a remote-path variant.
fix_summary: Change signature to `func (p *Phase) GenerateTerraformVars(ctx context.Context, cfg *config.Config, opts *Options) error`. Single caller at setup/steps.go:234 already has ctx via the StepDef Exec closure.
must_preserve: 0o600 permission bits; atomic-write semantics via renderAndWrite.

smell: cleanup.InstalledPackages and cleanup.InstalledBinaries are exported but their only callers are the package-private Packages() function at line 66 and 72. No external caller in-tree. They are shaped like 'query what cleanup would remove', which is a plausible future CLI surface (e.g. `okdctl cleanup preview`), so this fits scaffolding.
severity_reason: Scaffolding: shaped like a symmetric 'preview/plan' helper for a future `okdctl cleanup preview` verb. Not currently consumed.
fix_summary: Verify intent — if a preview/plan CLI verb is planned, keep and document. Otherwise unexport (installedPackages, installedBinaries).
rule_source: MEMORY.md §scaffolding (future-cli-verb: `okdctl cleanup preview` parallel to Packages)
must_preserve: The exact list values (coreos-installer, terraform for packages; openshift-install, oc, kubectl + ExternalToolBinaries for binaries).

smell: dns.BuildConfigData, dns.ConfigName, and dns.WriteDnsmasqConfig are exported but every caller is inside the dns package itself (DeployBootstrap/DeployProduction at dns.go:155, 197; WriteDnsmasqConfig at dns.go:156, 198). No external caller in-tree. Shaped like a 'build + write' split for test fakes or alternate drivers, but nothing uses them.
severity_reason: Not scaffolding-shaped — no matching Build/Read or ConfigName/Parse symmetry and no CLI-verb shape. Fine to unexport.
fix_summary: Unexport: buildConfigData, configName, writeDnsmasqConfig. Keep DeployBootstrap / DeployProduction as the package's external API. Three helpers become package-private.
rule_source: Uber §Exported Surface ('do not export without a caller')
must_preserve: DeployBootstrap and DeployProduction public behavior and their dnsmasq-restart rollback semantics.

smell: Two functions build a display status string via the same switch on (Skipped/Success/default) producing the literal values "skip"/"ok"/"fail". The value set is a three-state enum spelled inline in two places; adding a fourth state (e.g. "partial") would require editing both.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: duplicated 3-way switch producing stringly-typed output across two functions within the same file
fix_summary: Introduce a StepResult.DisplayStatus() method on distribution.StepResult returning a typed stepStatus (or even a plain enum with a String() method) so callers write `sb.kv(string(s.StepID), fmt.Sprintf("%-4s  %s", s.DisplayStatus(), d))` once. Alternatively hoist the switch into a local helper in summary.go.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: CSR.Pending is a boolean field that is unconditionally set to `true` by its only constructor (cluster.PendingCSRs) and never read anywhere. It is named to suggest tri-state (Pending/Approved/Denied) but the producer only emits Pending rows. Either the field is dead, or the CSR type should grow to carry the full conditions slice.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: field has no downstream reader and conveys no information — removing it is a one-line drop but the type is exported, so a consumer edit may be required
fix_summary: Delete the `Pending bool` field and the `Pending: true` assignment. The type name and constructor already convey that every returned CSR is pending. If a future consumer needs to distinguish states, introduce a CSRState enum (Pending/Approved/Denied) rather than a bool.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: LogLevel is a custom enum (Debug/Info/Warn/Error) that is not referenced anywhere — the package exposes Debug()/Info()/Warn()/Error() functions directly and uses charmlog.Level for level parsing. The enum is a premature abstraction that shadows log/slog's own leveling.
fix_summary: Delete the LogLevel type and its four constants. Callers wanting a typed level should import log/slog.Level directly (LevelDebug/LevelInfo/LevelWarn/LevelError) — that's also the seam audit-modernization will push toward.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: The if/else-if/else ladder around token assembly has an `if` branch whose body is a no-op (`_ = px.TokenID`). The comment explains the semantic (avoid "tokenid=tokenid=secret" double-prefix), but the empty-but-for-a-side-channel branch is an anti-pattern — invert the condition and either return early or drop the branch if the semantic is already covered by the else-if.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: semantic is correct but the shape (empty-then-else) is the kind of thing linters flag when they pick up the idiom
fix_summary: Collapse to: `if px.TokenID != "" && !strings.Contains(px.APIToken, "=") { token = px.TokenID + "=" + px.APIToken }`. Same behavior, no empty branch, no `_ = px.TokenID` dummy to confuse future readers.

smell: buildISOStrings and buildNodeNames in setup/terraform.go are structurally identical: allocate []string of length count, loop `for i := range count`, format `"%s:iso/%s%d.iso"` vs `"%s-%s%d"`. Both take (isoStorage/clusterName, phase.NodeRole, count). A single helper parameterized on the format string — or a quick tabular/template-driven approach — would de-duplicate. Low value today, but a new role (e.g. bastion-managed VM) doubles the edit.
fix_summary: Introduce `buildQuotedRoleList(format string, prefix string, role phase.NodeRole, count int) []string` that takes a format string with two %s + one %d and renders count elements. Both sites collapse to one-liners. Alternatively, accept the duplication as 'readable over clever' — the two names tell the reader more than a single generic helper would.
rule_source: Go proverb: A little copying is better than a little dependency (counter-argument to refactor — so this is a judgment call)

smell: Package distribution has two separate '// Package distribution ...' blocks (context.go:1 with a single sentence 'provides step-based provisioning orchestration' and step.go:1-5 with a multi-sentence description pointing at StepDef/StepBuilder/Orchestrator as canonical per CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes). godoc concatenates both, producing a double-intro with the terser one landing first and the canonical one second. Mirrors the prior doc:aa84670c (internal/cli) and doc:0934cf1b (internal/platform) findings from 2026-04-18 that were fixed — context.go was missed in that sweep.
fix_summary: Strip the '// Package distribution ...' block from context.go (it pre-dates step.go's richer block). Keep step.go as the sole package-doc site because it already carries the canonical-API pointer. No replacement comment needed — PhaseContext's own doc directly above the type is sufficient.
rule_source: Effective Go §Commentary — package comment 'appears in the first file of the package that has a comment'
must_preserve: step.go's reference to CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (StepDef canonical) — do not collapse into the terser context.go block.

smell: `if dotsNeeded < 3 { dotsNeeded = 3 }` is a hand-rolled `max(dotsNeeded, 3)`. Go 1.21's `max` builtin is ordered-type generic and collapses the three-line floor into a one-line assignment; the same pattern repeats in at least five other sites (download/progress.go, tui/layouts.go, doctor.go) so a uniform rewrite is cheap.
fix_summary: Replace with `dotsNeeded := max(keyColWidth - keyLen - 2, 3)`. `max` is a Go 1.21 builtin, works on any ordered type, no import needed. Drops 3 lines to 0 and removes the intermediate mutation.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever
must_preserve: Minimum-3-dots floor for dotted KV rendering (keeps the separator visually distinct when the key column is tight).

smell: Two adjacent hand-rolled floor/ceiling clamps (`if pct > 1 { pct = 1 }` and `if barWidth < 4 { barWidth = 4 }`) replicate the exact shape `min` and `max` were added (Go 1.21) to express. `min(pct, 1.0)` and `max(barWidth, 4)` read faster and delete the intermediate mutations.
fix_summary: Replace with `pct := min(float64(pw.written)/float64(pw.total), 1.0)` and `barWidth := max(pw.width - len(pw.desc) - 12, 4)`. Go 1.21 builtins, no import. Drops 6 lines to 0 (each 3-line if becomes a single-expression max/min).
must_preserve: Rendered bar never exceeds 100% (pct clamp) and never degenerates to zero width (barWidth floor) — both are rendering-invariant.

smell: Two identical `if sev > worst { worst = sev }` blocks in the same function (`checkBinaries`) are hand-rolled `worst = max(worst, sev)` — `severity` is a named `int` (line 34), and Go 1.21's generic `max` accepts ordered named types without adaptation.
fix_summary: Replace both `if X > worst { worst = X }` blocks with `worst = max(worst, X)`. `max` works on `severity int` directly (verified empirically). Drops 6 lines to 2 and removes the branch — the running-max is what the code already meant.
rule_source: Go 1.21 release notes: min/max builtins on ordered types
Go spec: named types inherit underlying ordering
must_preserve: Highest-severity-wins aggregation across all probed binaries; `worst` must still equal `sevFail` when any required binary is missing.

smell: Executor only sets cmd.Env when len(e.Env) > 0, otherwise the subprocess inherits the parent's full environment — including PROXMOX_PASSWORD, PULL_SECRET, PROXMOX_API_TOKEN, and any other credentials the operator exported. A bug or malicious wrapper in terraform / openshift-install / oc plugins could leak these into argv-visible children (e.g. via /proc/self/environ readable by same-uid processes).
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — every exec.Command call that doesn't explicitly configure env inherits credentials; the canonical wrapper is the place to fix this once.
fix_summary: Always set cmd.Env explicitly. Build a minimal base (PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM, KUBECONFIG, PROXMOX_*, TF_* allowlist) via an env-allowlist applied by default. Extend WithEnv to be additive on top of the allowlist rather than optional. Document the escape hatch WithInheritedEnv for the one or two callers (doctor, install monitor) that legitimately need full inheritance.
must_preserve: KUBECONFIG propagation used by install.SetupKubeconfig; TerraformEnv plumbing via WithEnv; password-scrubbing invariants in internal/credentials.

smell: configureSELinuxForApache discards both the result and error of two semanage port invocations via '_, _ = p.Exec.Run(...)'. The comment 'Try -a first; if port already exists, -m modifies' covers the expected case, but any other semanage failure (policy not loaded, selinux in disabled state, perms) is invisible — apache then silently binds 8080 with no SELinux label and may later refuse connections.
fix_summary: Capture result of the -m call and log result.Stderr at warn level if exit != 0. The -a fallback-to-error pattern is fine, but the final state should be checked; a single 'semanage port -l | grep 8080' probe would confirm the policy was applied and surface any real failure.
rule_source: Go proverb: errors are values — handle them
repo counter-example: p.Log.Warn on apache.configureApachePort failures
must_preserve: the -a then -m ordering (first-add-then-modify) must stay to handle both fresh and pre-labeled hosts.

smell: NewInsecure returns an HTTP client with InsecureSkipVerify=true, narrowly scoped to bootstrap-phase probes per the doc comment. No test locks that New() does NOT return an insecure client (i.e. the TLS config is nil or has InsecureSkipVerify=false). A refactor that factories out a shared transport could silently flip the invariant.
severity_reason: The invariant "New() is secure" is intuitive but worth locking. A regression would defeat TLS verification on every HTTP call the repo makes — but the caller landscape is small and the gosec suppression is present, so the blast radius is bounded.
fix_summary: TestNewVsNewInsecure: c := New(1*time.Second); assert c.Transport is nil (Go uses DefaultTransport which validates); d := NewInsecure(1*time.Second); assert d.Transport.(*http.Transport).TLSClientConfig.InsecureSkipVerify is true. Three assertions, no live network.
must_preserve: New() has no custom Transport; NewInsecure() HAS InsecureSkipVerify=true.
